Q: Which factor commonly causes slow speeds on a wired link?
Option2: Duplex or speed mismatch between the switch and the network interface card (NIC)

Q: What does a limited connectivity status usually mean?

Q: Poor Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP) quality is most directly tied to which metrics?
Option2: Latency, jitter, and packet loss - improve with Quality of Service (QoS) and stable links

Q: What is port flapping on a switch?
Option2: Link rapidly goes up and down due to bad cabling, auto-negotiation issues, or failing hardware

Q: Which cause often produces high latency on a path?
Option2: Congestion, long distance, or queuing - use path tests and Quality of Service (QoS)

Q: Which household device commonly creates interference near 2.4 GHz?

Q: A wired client connects at 100 Mbps instead of 1 Gbps. First check?
Option2: Cable quality (Category 5e or Category 6), connectors, and auto-negotiation settings

Q: A user receives an Automatic Private IP Addressing (APIPA) address 169.254.x.x. What does this imply?
Option1: Healthy Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP) service
Option2: Client could not reach the Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP) server - check scope, relay, and connectivity

Q: Which action helps stabilize voice and video across a mixed network?
Option2: Enable Quality of Service (QoS) markings and prioritize real-time traffic while monitoring for jitter and loss
